evidence: Written mathematical arguments, separate internal AI reviews, and supplementary exact computational controls. Not externally peer reviewed or formally verified.
novelty: Bounded primary-source and later-literature searches found no exact prior resolutions; historical novelty is not established.
catalog_policy: Five affirmative proofs and two counterexamples receive repository-local solved statuses. The two conditional algorithmic conclusions remain partial, as does the commuting-support theorem.

results.title: High-precision low-rank tensor optimization
results.result: NP-hardness already at CP rank at most two, mode size two, zero sparse term and positive bounded rational factors. A deterministic algorithm with the requested logarithmic precision dependence would imply P=NP in the binary rational-input model. The same construction gives a uniform-marginal MOT hardness corollary.
results.boundary: The hardness theorem is unconditional. The negative algorithmic conclusion is conditional on P != NP; no complexity-class separation is proved.
results.primary_location: §6.7.2, discussion after Theorem 6.7.4, p.190. Search-qualified status: Explicitly open in thesis and associated papers. Targeted later searches found numerical and structural advances but no resolution of these precise complexity questions.
results.internal_review: accepted by a second AI research agent; not external peer review

results.title: Brownian power-integral conditioning
results.result: Under the canonical density disintegration, the Brownian path conditioned on one power integral being zero converges to the zero path in the uniform topology. Every fixed-radius escape probability decays faster than any prescribed exponential in the power.
results.boundary: Exact single-integral question only; the full-signature and comparison questions Q191 and Q193 remain unresolved.

results.title: Bunkbed inequality for transitive tournaments
results.result: The independent-edge, bidirectional-vertical bunkbed inequality holds for every transitive tournament. The proof allows any common horizontal retention probability and independent vertex-dependent vertical probabilities; at probability one half the gap for u<v is at least 2^(-(v-u+2)).
results.boundary: Transitive tournaments and the stated independent-edge model. Arbitrary acyclic graphs and conditioned paired-edge models are outside the result.

results.title: Scissors support in multiplayer equilibrium
results.result: Every mixed Nash equilibrium of the source three-action imbalanced rock-paper-scissors game has at least two players assigning positive probability to scissors, for every integer m>=2.
results.boundary: Exact three-action game; no claim for the source's larger blown-up action spaces.

results.title: Negative-covariance minimizers
results.result: Four explicit bounded, centered, two-point marginals have unrestricted minimum 16 and minimum 920/57 under pairwise nonpositive covariances. Every unrestricted minimizer has Cov(X2,X3)>=1/2. Nondegenerate counterexamples extend to every n>=4.
results.boundary: The quadratic objective is the maximum over all subsets with the exact heterogeneous marginals in the report. Both optima have rational certificates.

results.title: Realizing factorial-language complexity
results.result: The factor-closed language 0*1* union {10} has complexity 2,4,4,5,6,... . A plateau in recurrent-factor complexity must persist, so no infinite binary word has this complexity at every length.
results.boundary: Disproves the exact all-length equality in Conjecture 6.36; no claim about eventual equality or separate permutation-class growth-rate conjectures.

results.title: Exact Fatou and invariance of sum quasinorms
results.result: The actual infimum sum quasinorm of the source rearrangement-invariant Fatou quasi-Banach function spaces is exactly rearrangement invariant and has the exact Fatou property on every sigma-finite resonant measure space.
results.boundary: Full source scope, including infinite measure and equal-mass atomic spaces. Attainment is not needed; an auxiliary example shows it can fail on a nonatomic space.

results.title: Continuity of Moore-Penrose inversion
results.result: When corresponding initial support idempotents commute and corresponding final support idempotents commute, M||a-b||<1 forces equal supports and ||b^dagger-a^dagger|| <= ||b^dagger||||a^dagger||||a-b||, where M=max(||a^dagger||,||b^dagger||).
results.boundary: The unrestricted noncommuting-support conjecture remains open. The result removes the ultrahermitian assumption in the specified commuting setting; strict separation of algebra classes is not claimed.
results.internal_review: accepted by a second AI research agent; not external peer review

results.title: Connected-set evaluation at minus two
results.result: Exact C_G(-2) evaluation is #P-hard by an explicit polynomial-size single-call reduction and belongs to GapP; it is polynomial-time computable if and only if FP=#P. Rooted attachments also classify every nonzero fixed algebraic evaluation point as #P-hard.
results.boundary: The signed function is not called #P-complete. No separation FP != #P is proved; exact algebraic outputs use a fixed-number-field bit model.

results.title: Periodic zero-extension in numeration
results.result: For every p>=1, validity is preserved and reflected by appending p zeroes exactly when maximal greedy words are nested along residue classes modulo p. Their unique infinite limits satisfy every stated cross-residue lexicographic shift inequality.
results.boundary: Full Conjecture 9.1 for positional U-systems; the separate alternate-base and noncanonical-shift conjectures are not resolved.
